exposure: Planned place of birth (hospital labour ward, birth centre, home)
outcome: Interventions and procedures during labour and birth
Admission to special care/high dependency or intensive care units (mother or infant)
Perinatal mortality (intrapartum stillbirth and neonatal death)
cohort: 1,251,420 Australian women with uncomplicated pregnancies who gave birth between 2000 and 2012 to a singleton baby in cephalic presentation at between 37 and 41 completed weeks' gestation
finding: Planned births in birth centres or at home were associated with higher odds of normal labour and birth compared to planned hospital births, with no significant differences in perinatal mortality rates observed.
mod_finding: For healthy women in Australia having an uncomplicated pregnancy, planned births in birth centers or at home are associated with positive maternal outcomes.
